sourceScope: Source and selected exact preview artifact; no server/device mutations
securityScan: NOT_VERIFIED: managed tool failure; no replacement scan

dataFlows.originSendStore: Signup inputs → Supabase Auth over HTTPS; first_name/last_name/full_name/city in Auth metadata; linked app account/profile. Session/refresh state uses AsyncStorage.
dataFlows.visibility: Own authenticated session; public profile exposes intended name/city fields, not a blanket permission to expose email.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Logout clears session-related caches. Closure blanks app email/phone/name/city and profile fields, then Auth soft-deletes identity and verifies metadata/password/session outcome; pseudonymous UUID/audit retained. Mail-provider retention not established.

dataFlows.originSendStore: User picker/camera → authenticated media Edge → orientation-aware sanitization → private profile-media bucket; profile holds reference.
dataFlows.visibility: Authorized profile/avatar reads via RPC/media worker; must not infer all Storage objects are public.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Clear/discard exists. Closure schedules owned unprotected Storage deletion before relational wipe; scoped evidence may be held. EXIF/GPS stripped, but pixels may still reveal a face/address.

dataFlows.originSendStore: User text/map/GPS and confirmed location review → owned RPC/private location structures. Typed/reverse query → LocationIQ EU endpoint. Structured address/access notes and free-text history may also reach Gemini.
dataFlows.visibility: Owner review; selected bilateral Agreement private location requires grant/readback and expires/revokes with session/participant/state; public map is a separate approximate projection.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Closure erases private location/need-sensitive material and address-containing AI rows except narrowly protected material. No proof that provider-side logs/backups are erased by app closure.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Confirmed city/area/public geography → needs/profile matching/discovery. Client fetches OpenFreeMap map assets, revealing network/view-area metadata to tile service; explicit external map opening sends coordinates to Google Maps.
dataFlows.visibility: Task discovery and profile matching readers; no assumption of anonymous visibility beyond actual readers.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Closure blanks approximate city/area/lat/lng and profile city/area fields; external map provider requests have separate retention.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Typed text → owned Agreement/group RPC → public.agreement_messages/private.group_messages_v5 plus visibility rows. UI resolves sender name/avatar.
dataFlows.visibility: Bilateral requester/selected worker; task group membership and per-message visibility. Participants cannot create private conversations with each other through this model; canceled member future access is restricted.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Closure replaces author body, removes photo references, clears ordinary group body; selected support snapshots may remain as separate protected evidence. Recipient copies/exports outside app cannot be retroactively erased.
dataFlows.source: Erasure migration:227,314–318; `src/data/conversationInboxClientService.ts`; connected lifecycle evidence described below.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Picker/camera → media Edge sanitizes → private Storage and asset metadata. Task publication evaluator can send selected sanitized JPEG bytes inline to Gemini.
dataFlows.visibility: Task publication decides public photo projection; Agreement photo endpoint is scoped to Agreement/message. Profile avatar is a separate scope; worker AI has no task-photo attachment mandate.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Remove/cancel/discard and closure object-first deletion exist. Strip metadata does not remove private information visibly photographed. Provider retention for image review is unverified.

dataFlows.originSendStore: User input + up to30 history messages (each capped4000chars) + allowed structured facts/candidate → Edge → Gemini. Durable AI messages/proposals/reviews/commands in private/public AI tables.
dataFlows.visibility: Owner conversation, service AI processing; confirmed public task/profile is separately reviewed, not all raw chat public.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Ordinary closure erases/redacts AI conversation/facts/proposals/review envelopes; active turn and evidence conditions block unsafe closure. Provider retention/training contract is not inferred from code.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Held foreground PCM → speech session/proxy/Google transient transcription → text draft/chat. This is distinct from Agreement voice recording.
dataFlows.visibility: User and speech processor; final transcript may enter durable AI history and its next provider context.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: No app audio archive intended for AI transcription; provider transient/security retention not verified. Existing VOICE_PROCESSING_NOTICE still mentions removed voice mode/auto-send and must be reconciled with actual behavior.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Foreground recording → explicit send/upload → authenticated media Edge → agreement-voice private bucket (.m4a), asset metadata and message reference.
dataFlows.visibility: Authorized Agreement participants via authenticated binary playback, not a public/signed URL.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Private local cache is retired with session; server audio persists for conversation until applicable deletion. Closure worker explicitly supports agreement-voice objects. Therefore blanket “USKOČI never stores audio” is false outside AI-only scope.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Completion-based rating RPC → private.agreement_reviews → role/account reputation projection. Optional comment v2 → private.agreement_review_comments_v1.
dataFlows.visibility: Authorized/public reputation projection; comments reader respects moderation/block rules. D12 build flag is absent in checked-in production env, so do not automatically claim every final build enables comments; remote env remains unknown.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Author closure erases comment; target closure/moderation can hide while retaining another author's comment. Numeric/shared reputation and pseudonymous relation require declared retention. Existing candidate header “NOT APPLIED” is historical; use current ledger for status.

dataFlows.originSendStore: User targets account/task/Agreement with category/reason/narrative → owned report RPC → restricted safety/support records and deliberate evidence snapshots.
dataFlows.visibility: Reporter/authorized support workflows; not a public feed. User block is separate from moderation decision.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Closure has named scoped/media/history/shared-decision exceptions. Ordinary unrelated profile/chat must not be retained just because a case exists; final closure waits for exception resolution. Who resolves, under what period/SLA and appeal path is not proven.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Explicit device connection/permission → Expo token → account-owned registration/rotation RPC → notification_push_devices/preferences and attempts. Service sends token + generic title/body + opaque event identity to Expo/FCM/APNs.
dataFlows.visibility: Account/device and internal transport; message body/private address is not placed in the shown push payload. Lock-screen channel PRIVATE.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Deactivate/rotate supported. Closure deletes tokens/preferences/attempts/delivery rows. Expo ticket/receipt success is not device delivery. Current production registration lacks its Firebase client.

dataFlows.originSendStore: Owned request → bounded export worker → private data-export-artifacts → authenticated binary download with generation/size/hash/expiry checks. Journals store opaque request coordinates for uncertain writes.
dataFlows.visibility: Account owner; support/audit functions narrowly authorized; download never enabled by mere intake receipt.
dataFlows.retentionDeleteLimits: Artifact revoke/expiry and closure deletion precede final Auth erasure. User-saved export leaves app control. Minimal pseudonymous command/security records may remain; numerical legal periods not proven by source alone.
